answers.assumption_check: Assumed, and measured only at n=2: the refusal is the missing seal alone (35bb99574043 and 1eeeab70c59e both print the same exit-2 line before any proof runs), so nothing shows yet whether those proofs would pass under a seal. Assumed and unmeasured: that the Windows seal of 56b61c10bdbe, once built, is what the gate's re-run needs; the build re-reads that ticket's state before choosing between waiting on it and a gate-side change. The mechanism is a hypothesis, not a settled design.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs and has: the refusal line quoted verbatim in the ticket; the gate (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py, which runs the instrument through bin/cairn test); the seal ticket 56b61c10bdbe to read before building; the proof location (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/proofs/, red-first, PROVES declared, one tooth per clause); and that Windows cannot seal, so any seal of the proof is a Linux hand's. It lacks which hand a Windows verdict should be; the ticket says so and the how is labelled a hypothesis.
answers.children: none, because the work is one gate behavior and its proof: cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py
answers.collision_check: Possible overlap, not collision, with 56b61c10bdbe (the Windows instance seal, at TICKETME): that ticket builds the seal, this one proves the verdict gate's re-run uses it. If 56b61c10bdbe lands first and this ticket's proof is green with no gate change, this closes as proved by its proof. The precedent 3a38e2e1cfe0 (Windows clause verdicted on Linux) is a hand, not a rule; nothing in the Laws forbids either.
answers.falsifier_check: Falsifier: on Windows, the verdict gate's re-run of a green proof returns exit 0 and the artifact lands, and a red proof verdicts fail; today the same call exits 2 with the instance-seal refusal. Horizon: the next Windows ticket with a Windows-only clause verdicts on its own box.
answers.gates_bound: proved (Law 8: a proof a hollow build could not pass) and feeds back to origin on failure (Law 3): PROVEME runs the proof under the tester's seal on Linux; a red returns the ticket to FIXME.
answers.missing_check: Not wrapped: which hand a Windows verdict is (the gate's own run under a Windows seal, or a Linux hand as in 3a38e2e1cfe0). The ticket does not decide it; it names the measured gap and asks for a tooth that fails while a Windows verdict cannot re-run. No exemption is proposed: a refused re-run stays a refusal and the gate does not accept a builder's validate run in its place.

answers.title: a verdict run on Windows re-runs its instrument under a confirmed seal, so a Windows clause is judged by the gate and not only by the builder
answers.watchme: none, because its proof (the red-first proof its build adds under cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/proofs/) is the whole of its correctness, as for sibling ticket 56b61c10bdbe

bullets.text: A Windows verdict cannot re-run its instrument today: `cairn test --exec: refused — the instance seal is not confirmed (indeterminate: cannot build the instance seal: bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed); the command was not run`, exit 2. So a green-on-Windows clause is only ever measured by the builder's own validate run.
Instances: 3a38e2e1cfe0 (verdicted on Linux, PROVED 11-13), 35bb99574043 and 1eeeab70c59e (refused 2026-11-19). Related, not duplicated: 56b61c10bdbe.

title: a verdict run on Windows re-runs its instrument under a confirmed seal, so a Windows clause is judged by the gate and not only by the builder
